$comment: Built-in test switch catalog. Metadata only — behavior lives in src/lab/engine/switches.ts, keyed by id. kind: simulate = changes what you see; analyze = overlays measurements and findings; guide = a check the browser cannot emulate from a page, with exact manual steps. sameOrigin: true when the switch needs DOM access to the frame (production must go through the proxy for these to apply).

switches.label: Color vision
switches.description: Simulates color vision deficiency with the Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes (2009) model, applied in linear RGB — the same model Chrome DevTools uses. Anomalous options interpolate toward the dichromat matrix and are approximations.

switches.label: Low acuity
switches.description: Gaussian blur as a rough proxy for uncorrected refractive error. Not a clinical simulation — use it to judge whether hierarchy and key actions survive blur.

switches.label: Glare / low contrast
switches.description: Reduces contrast to approximate bright sunlight on a phone, a dim projector or cataracts. A design that only just passes 4.5:1 falls apart here.

switches.label: Text spacing override
switches.description: Applies the WCAG 1.4.12 values: line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em. Pair with the Reflow & clipping check to catch truncated or overlapping text.

switches.label: Root text size
switches.description: Raises the root font size, which only grows type set in rem/em. Text that does not grow is set in px — it will still grow with browser zoom (use the zoom control for 1.4.4), but not with a user's default font size preference.

switches.label: Pseudo-localization
switches.description: Rewrites visible text to stress the layout the way translation does. Expansion adds ~40% length (W3C i18n: many languages run 30%+ longer than English); long words mimic German compounds.

sources.label: W3C i18n: text size in translation

switches.label: Images off
switches.description: Replaces every image with its alt text in a box, as a slow connection or a blocked CDN would. Shows what the page says without pictures.

switches.label: Force reduced motion
switches.description: Forces animations and transitions to finish instantly. It shows what the page looks like with motion removed; it does NOT test whether the design honors prefers-reduced-motion — the Media feature support check and the OS setting do that.

switches.label: Keyboard only
switches.description: Disables pointer input inside the frame so you have to reach everything with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys. Click into the frame once to give it focus.

switches.label: Focus tracker
switches.description: Draws a high-visibility ring around whatever has focus inside the frame, so you can tell when a component's own focus style is missing or obscured.

switches.label: Tab order
switches.description: Numbers every keyboard stop in sequential focus order and connects them. Positive tabindex and order that jumps against reading order are flagged.

switches.label: Target size
switches.description: Measures interactive targets. Under 24×24 CSS px fails 2.5.8 (AA) unless the spacing exception applies — the exception is not evaluated, so check those by eye. Under 44×44 is flagged against 2.5.5 (AAA) and platform guidance.

switches.label: Headings outline
switches.description: Labels h1–h6 and role=heading in place and lists the outline. Flags skipped levels, missing or multiple h1 and empty headings.

switches.label: Landmarks
switches.description: Outlines banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, search, form and region landmarks. Flags a missing main and duplicate unlabeled navigation.

switches.label: Alt text
switches.description: Shows each image's alt text in place. Missing alt fails; empty alt is marked decorative; filename-like alt is flagged.

switches.label: Accessible names
switches.description: Shows the approximate accessible name of every button, link and form control (aria-labelledby, aria-label, label, content, title). Flags controls with no name. Approximate — the full accname algorithm has more cases; confirm doubtful ones with a screen reader.

switches.label: Text contrast
switches.description: Measures every visible text run against its effective background (semi-transparent layers composited). WCAG 2.x ratio decides pass/fail; APCA Lc is shown as a WCAG 3 draft second opinion. Text over images or gradients is reported as unknown, never as a pass.

switches.label: axe-core audit
switches.description: Runs Deque's axe-core rules engine (the engine behind Lighthouse's accessibility score) inside the frame. Automated rules catch roughly a third to a half of WCAG issues — a clean run is necessary, not sufficient.

switches.label: Reflow & clipping
switches.description: Flags horizontal page scroll and elements whose text is clipped by overflow. Run it at 320 CSS px (1280 at 400% zoom) for 1.4.10, and with the text spacing override for 1.4.12.

switches.label: Grid overlay
switches.description: Overlays a spacing grid for checking rhythm and alignment against the spec.

switches.label: Fold lines
switches.description: Marks where the first, second and third screens end at the current viewport height.

switches.label: Element outlines
switches.description: Outlines every element — the classic CSS debugging pass for spotting stray margins, overflow and nesting.

switches.label: Squint test
switches.description: Heavy blur plus reduced contrast. What still stands out is your visual hierarchy; if the primary action disappears, the hierarchy is wrong.

switches.label: Grayscale
switches.description: Removes hue so you can see whether state, status or meaning relies on color alone.

switches.label: Reading level
switches.description: Flesch-Kincaid grade of the visible body copy, per block and for the page. 3.1.5 (AAA) asks for supplemental content beyond lower secondary level (about grade 9). English only; the syllable count is heuristic.

switches.label: Media feature support
switches.description: Scans the frame's stylesheets for prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, forced-colors and pointer/hover rules. Tells you whether the design adapts to user settings at all, before you test how well.

switches.label: Nielsen heuristics
switches.description: Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics as a scored checklist for this screen. Each pass or fail you mark is saved as evidence on the open hypothesis.

switches.label: Theme
switches.description: Sets light or dark by toggling the .dark class and color-scheme on the frame's root. Designs that only respond to prefers-color-scheme need the manual Emulate media check.

switches.label: Right-to-left
switches.description: Sets dir=rtl on the frame root. Logical properties (ms-, ps-, start/end) should mirror; physical left/right will not.

switches.label: Forced colors
switches.description: Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode cannot be emulated from a page.
guide: Open the design in its own tab (Open frame).
Chrome DevTools → ⋮ → More tools → Rendering → Emulate CSS media feature forced-colors: active.
Check focus indicators, icons drawn with background-image, and borders that relied on box-shadow — those vanish.
On Windows: Settings → Accessibility → Contrast themes → Aquatic, for a real check.

switches.label: Emulate user preferences
switches.description: prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast and prefers-color-scheme can only be emulated by the browser, not by a page.
guide: Open the design in its own tab (Open frame).
Chrome DevTools → Rendering → Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Motion that remains should be essential or under 5 seconds and pausable.
Same panel: prefers-contrast: more, and prefers-color-scheme: dark.
Run Media feature support first — if a feature has zero rules, the design ignores that setting.

switches.label: Screen reader pass
switches.description: No automated tool tells you what a screen reader user experiences. Do a short pass on the real thing.
guide: Open the design in its own tab (Open frame).
macOS: VoiceOver (Cmd+F5). Rotor (VO+U) → Headings and Landmarks: do they describe the page on their own?
Windows: NVDA (free). H / D to jump headings / landmarks, Tab through controls, listen to each name and state.
Trigger every dynamic change (carousel, menu, form error) and confirm it is announced once, meaningfully.
Log what you hear as an observation — that is the evidence.
